expectations.text: Refuses to validate the shift of retargeting to 65% of spend
expectations.evidence: "Verdict: Reject the 42% → 65% retargeting shift." and "Bottom line for approval purposes: approve a bounded test ... not the 65/35 split as pitched."

expectations.text: States retargeting's reported ROAS is structurally inflated and largely non-incremental (many of those users would have converted anyway)
expectations.evidence: "Retargeting ROAS is structurally inflated by design, not by this buyer's skill. It's built from people who already visited the site, added to cart, or engaged with the brand — a meaningful share of them would have bought anyway, with or without the ad."

expectations.text: Identifies the current 42% retargeting share as already above the ~40% alarm threshold
expectations.evidence: "Retargeting above ~40% of spend is itself a warning signal, not a success signal. Pellagrino is already past that line at 42%."

expectations.text: States that retargeting above ~40% of spend is a signal to grow prospecting, not evidence that retargeting works
expectations.evidence: The transcript only says crossing 40% is "a warning signal, not a success signal" and "should already have triggered a review" — it never explicitly frames the threshold as a signal to grow prospecting specifically.

expectations.text: Cites the reference starting split: 70-80% prospecting, 15-25% retargeting, remainder experimental
expectations.evidence: No such reference split appears anywhere; the transcript's thresholds are "≥60% of spend" for prospecting and "~40%" for retargeting, with no mention of a 70-80/15-25/experimental baseline.

expectations.text: Explains that warm pools are refilled by colder tiers, so cutting prospecting starves the retargeting refill
expectations.evidence: "The retargeting pool is fed by prospecting traffic. Cut prospecting by ~40% ($34.8k → $21k) and the pool that generates the 9.4x starts shrinking within weeks ... the buyer would be starving the input to the exact tier he's trying to scale."

expectations.text: Notes the retargeting pool decays to nothing within weeks once the refill stops
expectations.evidence: The transcript says "a retargeting pool decays fast once the refill slows" and the pool "starts shrinking within weeks," but never states it decays to nothing/is exhausted — only that shrinkage begins.

expectations.text: Recommends moving the split back toward prospecting (inside the 15-25% retargeting band) rather than further away
expectations.evidence: The counter-proposal instead allows retargeting to rise modestly from 42% ("move it up in small steps ... 42% → ~47-50%"), moving further from, not back toward, any 15-25% retargeting band.

expectations.text: Warns that over-funding retargeting inflates blended ROAS
expectations.evidence: "Comparing the two head-to-head and funding the winner is exactly the move that inflates blended numbers while quietly starving the thing feeding the pool."

expectations.text: Recommends an incrementality check (e.g. a holdout) before crediting retargeting's ROAS
expectations.evidence: "Run an incrementality test on retargeting first (platform conversion-lift tool or a simple holdout). This is the only honest way to know if 9.4x is real or mostly non-incremental."

expectations.text: States retargeting must not be used to prove the plan works
expectations.evidence: "Retargeting is also explicitly not the tier you use to prove a plan is working, because its number isn't a clean read of incremental value — it's a mix of true incremental sales and sales that were coming regardless."

expectations.text: Names prospecting share of spend (hold at or above ~60%) as an ongoing KPI
expectations.evidence: "Prospecting share should hold at ≥60% of spend as a standing health metric, unless the brand is deliberately harvesting down a shrinking pool for a defined reason" and "Never let prospecting drop below ~55-60% of spend."

expectations.text: Refuses to validate the shift of retargeting to 65% of spend
expectations.evidence: "Don't approve this as written." and later: "the direction... may well be right, but 42%→65% in one move, justified by raw ROAS comparison, is the kind of decision that looks great in month 1 and shows up as a revenue and customer-growth problem in month 2-3."

expectations.text: States retargeting's reported ROAS is structurally inflated and largely non-incremental (many of those users would have converted anyway)
expectations.evidence: "Retargeting ROAS is inflated by selection bias... A meaningful share of those 9.4x 'attributed' sales would have converted anyway via direct traffic, brand search, or email, with zero ad spend. Platform ROAS... takes credit for demand it didn't create."

expectations.text: Identifies the current 42% retargeting share as already above the ~40% alarm threshold
expectations.evidence: The transcript never mentions a ~40% alarm threshold or frames the current 42% split as already problematic in itself; it only discusses the proposed jump to 65%.

expectations.text: States that retargeting above ~40% of spend is a signal to grow prospecting, not evidence that retargeting works
expectations.evidence: No mention of a 40% threshold or this framing anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: Cites the reference starting split: 70-80% prospecting, 15-25% retargeting, remainder experimental
expectations.evidence: No such reference split is cited; the transcript only discusses the current 42%/58% split and the proposed 48-50%/65% figures.

expectations.text: Explains that warm pools are refilled by colder tiers, so cutting prospecting starves the retargeting refill
expectations.evidence: "The retargeting pool is fed by prospecting. Cutting prospecting from 58%... to 35%... means far fewer new site visitors and cart events."

expectations.text: Notes the retargeting pool decays to nothing within weeks once the refill stops
expectations.evidence: "Retargeting audiences decay in weeks. You will not get 65%-of-budget worth of qualified retargeting inventory; you'll hit frequency caps and audience exhaustion..."

expectations.text: Recommends moving the split back toward prospecting (inside the 15-25% retargeting band) rather than further away
expectations.evidence: The transcript instead recommends moving further toward retargeting, just less aggressively: "Something like 42% → 48-50% is a real test of the hypothesis without starving the funnel," not a reduction of retargeting share into a 15-25% band.

expectations.text: Warns that over-funding retargeting inflates blended ROAS
expectations.evidence: "acting on it at this scale will likely shrink your revenue and customer base even as the 'blended ROAS' number goes up."

expectations.text: Recommends an incrementality check (e.g. a holdout) before crediting retargeting's ROAS
expectations.evidence: "Get incremental ROAS before reallocating, not platform ROAS. Either a geo/audience holdout test (hold out ~10-20% of retargeting-eligible users, no ads, compare conversion) or a short conversion-lift test."

expectations.text: States retargeting must not be used to prove the plan works
expectations.evidence: No statement to this effect; closest is a recommendation to track leading indicators "not just blended ROAS," which is not the same claim.

expectations.text: Names prospecting share of spend (hold at or above ~60%) as an ongoing KPI
expectations.evidence: The transcript explicitly rejects a fixed-percentage floor: "Set a prospecting spend floor tied to new-to-file customers/month, not a fixed %, so retargeting can't structurally cannibalize its own supply."
